claims.text: Powder metallurgy can be used to incorporate graphene nanoplatelets into an HEA matrix.
Additive manufacturing can be used to incorporate graphene nanoplatelets into an HEA matrix.
A one-step synthesis route will produce a uniform dispersion of graphene nanoplatelets in the HEA.
Dispersed graphene nanoplatelets will promote formation of a continuous graphene-rich tribofilm during sliding.
The graphene-rich tribofilm will remain thermally stable over a broad service-temperature range.
Easy shear within the tribofilm will reduce interfacial friction.
The tribofilm will act as a protective barrier that limits material removal and lowers wear.
Graphene incorporation will reduce the coefficient of friction by approximately 30–50% relative to untreated HEA.
Graphene incorporation will reduce wear rate by approximately 30–50% relative to untreated HEA.
The reductions in friction and wear will be maintained across a wide service-temperature range.
Both frictional-heating and cold-wear mechanisms will be active over the proposed dry-sliding temperature range.
The untreated HEA has higher friction and wear, particularly at temperature extremes where standard lubrication mechanisms fail.
Avoiding graphene agglomeration is necessary for the predicted tribological benefits.
The intervention remains effective only if processing does not compromise other mechanical properties.
Processing-induced inhomogeneity or an unstable tribofilm can eliminate the predicted benefits.
The magnitude of improvement depends on processing parameters, graphene dispersion quality, and operating conditions.
Oxidation and other environmental factors may affect tribofilm stability.
